output.brief:
The rise in cancellations is mainly a Quillbook connector problem, not a pricing problem. Quillbook retired an old invoice interface on 30 March. Since then the connector has silently dropped or duplicated invoices. 58,300 invoices were affected across 1,212 accounts, and 34% of those accounts had cancelled by 31 July, against 8% of the Quillbook accounts with no recorded failure. Among accounts with no connector, churn is flat at about 1.9%, whether or not the price rose. Founders accounts, whose price did not change, churn as much as repriced ones on Quillbook. The seat-size pattern in the finance analysis is explained by larger accounts being more likely to use Quillbook. The failures were logged as warnings, so the health panel missed them.

Recommendation for the board: make the Quillbook v3 fix the top engineering priority, since it is a three to four week job. Contact every Quillbook account, including those that cancelled, to correct their invoices. Keep the duplicate-invoice hold on, because it protects customers' books. Don't reverse the price now, and hold off on the Tallymarsh rebuild. Review the Tallymarsh log first, because the evidence so far shows only small numbers. I'm fairly confident in this. The main gap is that the Tallymarsh log hasn't been reviewed.
